claim: START: Second Blender cycle: better involute gear teeth and coolant QD ports now that kit hierarchy tags exist; provisional visualisation under partner seeds

missed.issue: `allow_pcd_snap` can silently change the calculated pitch diameter, module, centre distance, or effective ratio merely to make a packaging seed look convenient.
missed.why_it_matters: This is the most likely source of a confidently wrong number: a visually plausible gear set can no longer be the solved planetary tooth set. In a planetary stage, an independently snapped PCD can also violate sun/planet/ring meshing and assembly centre-distance constraints.
missed.how_to_test: Generate the Blender geometry only from the tooth counts, module, pressure angle, and calculated pitch diameters emitted by `scripts/lib/fpk_gear_teeth.py`; fail the render/export if any displayed PCD differs from the solved value or if planetary mesh/centre-distance closure fails.

missed.issue: Increasing flank density and adding fillets is not sufficient to make a gear involute.
missed.why_it_matters: A sampled or cosmetically filleted tooth can appear involute while changing the active flank, base-circle intersection, root clearance, tooth thickness, and backlash. This silently changes behavior for any caller using the Blender output as dimensional reference rather than as a purely decorative render.
missed.how_to_test: Validate each tooth profile against the base-circle involute over its active flank, trim at specified addendum/root circles, and check tooth thickness/backlash at the pitch circle. Compare exported profile points with the source tooth-set parameters.

missed.issue: The proposed QD 'boss+collar+barb' compound assumes a universal quick-disconnect archetype.
missed.why_it_matters: QD ports vary by mating standard, seal arrangement, latch/collar travel, hose ID/OD, barb geometry, pressure rating, and service-access envelope. A decorative barb may imply hose compatibility or a disconnect mechanism that the intended coolant interface does not have.
missed.how_to_test: Require an explicit provisional interface record for each port: mating QD family, nominal bore, hose ID/OD, seal/latch representation, port orientation, and required coupling/un-coupling clearance. Render a mating-half and hose-envelope interference check, or label the feature as non-interface placeholder geometry.

missed.issue: Re-applying kit hierarchy after rendering may not be idempotent and may change object ownership, names, collections, or part counts for existing partner-seed assets.
missed.why_it_matters: `kit_parts>=17` can be satisfied by duplicated/tagged visualization objects rather than by the intended physical kit parts. This silently changes behavior for manifest consumers that treat collection membership or object names as authoritative BOM/hierarchy data.
missed.how_to_test: Run `scripts/motor-stack/apply_kit_hierarchy_manifest.py` twice against the same scene/manifest and diff the resulting manifest, collections, object identifiers, and kit count. Assert that visualization-only geometry cannot increment physical kit part count.

generality_concerns: Use `scripts/lib/fpk_gear_teeth.py` as the authoritative source for the calculated planetary tooth set; do not hand-derive or independently snap PCDs in Blender.
Use `scripts/motor-stack/apply_kit_hierarchy_manifest.py` rather than hand-editing hierarchy tags, and establish whether it is safe to run after Blender asset generation.

`pyleecan` may help independently inspect parameterized machine/gear-adjacent geometry, but it should not replace the repository's explicitly identified calculated tooth-set source without demonstrating parameter and convention equivalence.

The stated success criteria are visual/count criteria only. They do not establish gear conjugacy, planetary closure, QD mating compatibility, hose routing, or that hierarchy counts represent unique physical parts rather than render objects.
review.one_line_summary: Block `allow_pcd_snap` and cosmetic-only involute/QD work until Blender is constrained to the solved tooth set, QD interface assumptions are explicit, and hierarchy reapplication is proven idempotent.

reasoning_faults.consequence: Most likely path to a confidently wrong number: packaging-driven PCD changes silently invalidate tooth count, centre distance, or ratio while denser involute meshes still 'look right'.

reasoning_faults.consequence: Cosmetic Blender teeth/ports can diverge from the calculated/provisional seed topology the dossier already knows how to produce.

This is the assertion most likely to silently produce a confidently-wrong number.
review.one_line_summary: START intent claims gear-morphology and QD improvements as established, but the diff contains only planning docs; the QD half has no cited tool/standard and the PCD-snap approach risks contradicting the calculated tooth set.
missed: 1. 'allow_pcd_snap for packaging-seed tooth set' directly conflicts with the CALCULATION GUARD note that fpk_gear_teeth.py solves the planetary tooth set from the CALCULATED pitch diameters. Snapping PCD post-calculation can produce non-integer tooth counts and break the existing tooth-set invariant; the snap policy must be defined BEFORE the snap is allowed, not after.

2. 'Coolant QD reads as boss+collar+barb' is a geometric appearance criterion with no dimensional anchor. QD ports have mating-partner constraints (hose end, sealing face, flow area); without them the port will draw but not function. Needs a coupling-spec reference (e.g., ISO 7241-1 Series A/B, or a specific partner PN) before geometry is committed.

3. 'Blender' is named in the claim title but does not appear in the capability dossier's packages_available list. If the Blender Python API (bpy) is not actually importable in this environment, the cycle cannot execute and will silently no-op into a fake pass.

4. The success criterion 'kit_parts>=17' is asserted without derivation. Where does 17 come from? If it is the current count +1 from this cycle, that should be stated; if it is an absolute target, it needs justification.

5. The PROPOSED APPROACH lists 're-apply kit hierarchy' as a step after 're-render'. If apply_kit_hierarchy_manifest.py mutates the manifest based on current geometry, and the geometry is being changed in the same cycle, order matters and could overwrite tags added earlier in the cycle.
(b) Tools/solvers/corpus rows that should be used instead of hand-derivation:

1. scripts/lib/fpk_gear_teeth.py — the CALCULATION GUARD already says 'USE THE TOOL: ... apply_kit_hierarchy_manifest.py — do not hand-derive this', but the same principle applies to fpk_gear_teeth.py. Any involute flank density / fillet work must go through this, not be hand-tuned in Blender.

2. corpus: fpk_extracted_standards — should be queried for involute gear standards (ISO 6336 is referenced in explicitly_not_doing as the 'released set', but the calculation still needs module/profile-shift/addendum/dedendum limits from the standard, not from intuition).
3. corpus: fpk_extracted_claims and fpk_component_literature — should be checked for any prior partner-supplied QD spec or coolant-port claim that constrains the boss+collar+barb dimensions.
4. corpus: pretraining_extracted_specs — same reason; pretraining spec rows often carry manufacturer PN-to-dimension mappings for couplings.
5. If a flow/pressure sanity check is wanted on the QD port, ht (heat transfer) or CoolProp could size the bore, but neither is named in the approach — adding a flow check would close the loop.
(c) Single most likely way this stage produces a confidently-wrong number:

The PCD snap will round the calculated pitch diameter to a 'nice' value, which will then be fed back into fpk_gear_teeth.py to produce a tooth count. Because the tooth count is integer, the snap can quietly absorb up to ~0.5/module of pitch-diameter error into a wrong-but-plausible integer tooth count (e.g., 19 instead of 20). The downstream centre-distance and contact-ratio calculations will then propagate the error with full precision and high confidence, producing a gear mesh that looks correct in the visualisation but fails an ISO 6336 contact-ratio or interference check. This is the classic 'snapped-then-rounded-then-trusted' failure mode and should be guarded explicitly: log pre-snap and post-snap PCD, refuse the snap if it changes tooth count, and require a stated reason for any snap that does.
